title: Machine learning screening selects an energetic material for laboratory characterization
summary: A high-throughput workflow combined learned molecular-property predictions and crystal-packing classification to screen 25,112 generated structures and select ICM-104. The authors synthesized and characterized the selected material, reporting that its measured properties agreed with the model-assisted predictions. This is one laboratory-scale, study-specific material result; the broad candidate space remains computational, and the study does not establish scale-up, deployment or independent replication.
ai_technology: Machine-learning property regressors and a convolutional neural network for crystal-packing classification
organization: Institute of Chemical Materials, China Academy of Engineering Physics

evidence.tested: The study screened 25,112 generated candidates, selected one target material, then synthesized and characterized it; the publisher reports measured properties in agreement with predictions.
evidence.unknown: Only the selected target was synthesized and characterized. Scale-up, independent replication and operational performance are not established. Some energetic-performance values in the paper are calculated rather than directly measured.
evidence.ai_role: Learned molecular-property models and a CNN packing classifier helped rank and select the target for synthesis and characterization.

source_review.scope: Official publisher English article text/indexed conclusions and Chinese primary metadata/abstract reviewed; a saved 2026-11-16 review notes an author-hosted primary PDF was also checked.
